title: What a rule that never nests its fills keeps, and when it refills
claim: N1: a subdivision keeps k and lambda. N2: on a line with fills of triples keeping two orders, n <= (s0+1)(s1+1), with a full grid exactly when there are at most two middles and every allowed fill. N3: from a full grid, the never-nest rule with any old pairs (NNF) refills every new row or column forever. N4: from any line, NNF reaches a full grid before its first subdivision. N5: the corner rule across crossing splits (CC) keeps two orders, refills from a full grid, and never fills a line. N6 (proved after the read-out): under CC a split that crosses nothing never comes to cross one, so after one fill of a line CC reaches a full grid exactly when that fill's ends are the line's ends.
standard_statement: Greedy extension of split systems of a product of two chains by betweenness constraints; medians and corner completion in the grid.
